Now consider that the development costs also included proof of concepts for N64 prototype hardware, becoming proficient in programming the Playstation which, to date, their entire toolchain was assembly based (Tobal No. 1 was developed by Dreamfactory, not Square, and Playstation development necessitated C to include Sony's APIs), tooling up a CG video production studio along with 100% in-house artists and animators, It may still be considered one of the most expensive games made, but certainly not excessive considering it was about the same as Shenmue and Pokemon Red/Green.

trying to find a balance

That, that right there is the problem. Games, particularly iconic properties like Final Fantasy, should be unabashedly themselves. Compromise -- balance -- is where nobody is happy. Going action RPG for a game that was built around turn based combat isn't going to bring fans of the original around to action combat, and RPG action combat isn't going to attract FPS players. It sits in this compromised middle ground where it doesn't really try to stand out.

Square's best years were probably SNES / Playstation, as Squaresoft and Square Electronic Arts respectively (with the notable exception of Sony publishing FF7). They weren't the best years because there was nothing else enjoyable out there, they were the best years because they just made the games they wanted to make. They didn't care about attracting sports game fans or space shooter fans or platforming fans of the era. They had their niche and lived to serve that niche better than others did.

The cost of developing AAA titles continuing to skyrocket has lead to a paralyzing fear to not try to be something to everyone because otherwise they're just leaving money on the table.
